text:
Aisha: Heads-up — noticed a recurring pattern: mobile long-polling requests (keep-alive ~90–180s) are holding gateway connections and causing spikes in short-request latencies. Thinking about a policy to short-circuit very short requests to a fast lane and preempt long-poll sockets when pressure is high. Anyone seen similar? :thinking:
Ben: Can you paste the numbers? p50/p95/p99 for connection hold and request latency?
Aisha: Sure, quick snapshot from last hour:
```
requests: 420k
long-poll (hold > 60s): 3.8%
short requests p50: 12ms p95: 120ms p99: 450ms
spike windows correlate with long-poll saturation (conn count +40%)
```
Marco: Yeah we've seen this pattern on lower tiers. Two orthogonal approaches: admission control (reserve N fast slots per node) or short-circuit routing that treats < 1KB requests as ephemeral and places them on a separate accept queue.
Sophie: Big caution: short-circuiting affects retry semantics and side-effect safety. If we preempt a long-poll socket mid-handshake we must ensure upstream never sees duplicate side-effects. How do we mark idempotent vs stateful calls?
Eli: What if we use a two-path system: fast-path (stateless, idempotent OR read-only) + slow-path (persistent sockets). Route selection by header + content-length heuristic. If client doesn’t set header, default to slow-path. Also include a preemption token so long-poll can be resumed on slow-path or gracefully drained.
Ben: How would that work under overload? If all fast-path slots used, do we queue or degrade to slow-path? Queuing risks head-of-line blocking. Preempting existing long sockets seems safer but Sophie’s idempotency concern still stands.
Marco: Proposal: implement a soft-preempt mechanism — when fast-path pressure crosses threshold T, mark oldest long-poll eligible for preemption if it has sent a keepalive with resume token. Gateway sends a 102 Upgrade-like signal with resume token to client, then migrates request to slow-path handler. If client doesn’t reconnect within TTL we tear down. This keeps short requests moving.
Sophie: That requires client and SDK support for resume token. For third-party clients we need a fallback: accept that some preemptions are forced but log them and tie to a retry budget to avoid duplicate side-effects. Also add header X-Redwood-Idempotency-Opt-in.
Eli: We can minimize risk by requiring fast-path opt-in header (X-Prefer-Fast) for any request that might be preempted. Default remains safe slow-path. For mobile SDK we can flip header on chat heartbeats and ephemeral fetches.
Aisha: Implementation sketch + rollout plan:
- Phase 1: instrument fast/slow path counts + connection age metrics (canary on one region)
- Phase 2: add route config: max_fast_slots, preempt_threshold, resume_token_ttl
- Phase 3: client SDK opt-in + feature flag.
- Phase 4: enable soft-preempt with conservative thresholds, monitor errors and duplicate side-effects metric.
Marco: Sample route config we could add to ingress policy:
```yaml
routes:
  - match: path_prefix "/api/short"
    fast_path: true
    max_fast_slots: 120
    preempt_threshold_percent: 0.8
    resume_token_ttl: 30s
```
Ben: Metrics to track: number of preemptions, resume success rate, duplicate-sideeffect-rate, p99 short-path latency, accept-queue-length, conn-count by age bucket. Add an alert if duplicate-sideeffect-rate > 0.01%.
Sophie: Also need an audit log for preemptions for compliance and for developers to debug. And make sure billing attribution stays correct when a request hops between paths.
deploy-bot: Canary rollout for "fast-path" feature flag started in us-west-2 (canary=5% hosts).
Aisha: Great — I'll open an RFC with the config knobs and telemetry plan. For next steps: Marco, can you prototype the route config changes? Sophie, can you draft SDK opt-in semantics? Ben, help define the alert thresholds. I'll own instrumentation and the RFC. :thumbsup:
Ben: On it.
Marco: Will prototype a natty accept-queue + preempt handshake by EOW.
Sophie: Drafting SDK opt-in now, will include fallback semantics.
Eli: I'll mock the resume token wire format and share a tiny spec. :eyes:
Aisha: Thanks all — we'll review RFC in architecture review next week.
